Title: Pas members barred from backing Bersatu in Melaka polls
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas members will not be allowed to support Bersatu candidates in the upcoming Melaka state election if the party contests under its own logo.
Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party had confirmed it would contest at least one state seat in Melaka, where Bersatu was also fielding a candidate.
"If they use the Bersatu logo, our members will not be allowed to support them," he said.
Takiyuddin, who is also Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary-general, said yesterday that PN candidates would not clash with Umno or Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates in the Nov 14 election.
He said PN members had been instructed to support BN candidates, while BN members could also choose to support PN candidates.
On Oct 21, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition would contest 21 seats, while Pas and its allies would field candidates in the remaining seven, following the conclusion of seat negotiations.
He said BN would use its own logo, leaving it to Pas and its allies to decide which logo to use.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johari: Careful tenant selection key to community safety
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Homeowners should exercise greater care when renting out their properties to prevent overcrowding and disputes that could affect the safety and well-being of local communities.
Titiwangsa Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said problems could arise when homeowners who no longer lived in an area rented out their properties without properly considering the number of occupants and their suitability as tenants.
Citing past issues in Kampung Pandan, he said overcrowding in some homes had contributed to disputes and disturbances, including fights and gangsterism.
"At one time, many people lived in houses rented out by owners who no longer lived in the area. They lived in large numbers, leading to problems," he said at the Taman Angkat Amanita 2026 programme at the Laksamana People's Housing Project (PPR) in Jalan Peel here today.
He said he had worked with the Wangsa Maju district police chief to address the issues, including contacting homeowners and advising them to exercise greater care when selecting tenants.
"Through cooperation with the police, many of these problems were resolved. We contacted homeowners and advised them to be more careful when renting out their properties," he said.
Johari said maintaining public safety required close cooperation between the police, residents and community leaders, particularly in sharing information about potential risks.
He advised residents not to confront suspected criminals themselves, warning that doing so could put them in danger.
"Whatever crime residents know about, do not confront the criminals. Bring the information to my office so we can work out a strategy.
"I do not want overzealous residents to expose themselves to danger and become victims of criminals," he said.
Johari also encouraged residents, particularly those living in flats, to get to know their neighbours and remain alert to their surroundings.
"If we live on the seventh floor and there are 16 homes on that floor, we should, if possible, know all our neighbours.
"If we have not seen a neighbour for three or four days, we should check on them. If we are afraid to go on our own, inform the residents' association chairman," he said.
He urged youth non-governmental organisations to engage more actively with young people in densely populated housing areas, particularly PPR developments.
He said limited space at home meant young people often spent time on the ground floors of their blocks, making constructive activities important for strengthening community ties.
Youth groups, he added, could help young people build positive social networks and maintain stronger connections with their communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Terengganu Sultan's younger brother laid to rest
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, was laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum of Masjid Al-Muktafi Billah Shah here today.
The funeral rites for Tengku Baderul Zaman, 52, concluded at 6.10pm.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, attended the funeral, alongside Pahang's Tengku Ampuan, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, who was accompanied by her children to convey their condolences to the Terengganu royal family.
Also present were Terengganu State Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Mohd Nor Hamzah and state government leaders.
Earlier, the late Tengku Baderul Zaman's remains arrived at Sultan Mahmud Airport in Kuala Nerus at 1.20pm on a special aircraft before being taken to Balai Islam at Istana Syarqiyyah here at 2pm for mourners to pay their last respects.
After funeral prayers at Balai Islam, the remains were taken to the Royal Mausoleum, arriving at 5.03pm.
Terengganu Mufti Professor Dr Syed Hadzrullathfi Syed Omar led the recitation of Surah Yasin, followed by tahlil and prayers.
Tengku Baderul Zaman died at 1.20am today at Gleneagles Hospital in Kuala Lumpur. He leaves behind his widow, Toh Puan Seri Wan Hidayah Wan Ismail, and three children.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tun Faisal calls for Political Parties Act after PN deregistration row
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should introduce a Political Parties Act to regulate political parties separately from other organisations under the Societies Act 1966.
Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said the proposed legislation was needed following the dispute over the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) decision to deregister Perikatan Nasional (PN) earlier this week.
Tun Faisal questioned the RoS' independence from executive influence, despite Section 3(1) of the Societies Act 1966 stipulating that the Registrar is appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"There is a need to reform the laws and regulatory bodies governing political parties.
"The Act should go beyond the appointment of the Registrar and cover procedures for forming political coalitions, whether before or after elections," he said in a post on X today.
Tun Faisal said the proposed law should also require political parties to declare their assets, expenditure and political donations.
He also proposed setting up a special tribunal to resolve disputes involving party members, political parties and coalition partners.
Citing Kenya's Political Parties Act 2011, he said the country had established a selection committee comprising representatives of political parties, the legal fraternity and other stakeholders to oversee the appointment of its Registrar of Political Parties.
He said Malaysia should begin discussions involving political leaders and other stakeholders on introducing similar legislation as a long-term solution to political disputes.
On Tuesday,
the RoS revoked PN's registration
after finding that its explanation had failed to address the grounds for deregistration.
However, the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Thursday
granted PN a stay of the deregistration
pending a judicial review, allowing the coalition to contest the Nov 14 Melaka state election under its logo.
The RoS yesterday
filed an appeal
against the High Court's decision.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yeo Bee Yin: Consult experts before deciding on nationwide Waze ban
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should consult industry experts and navigation technology specialists before deciding whether to impose a nationwide ban on Waze.
Puchong MP Yeo Bee Yin, who is also DAP national publicity secretary warned that a hasty decision could disrupt millions of Malaysians who rely on the application for daily commutes, logistics and their livelihoods.
"We urge the National Security Council to consult industry experts and navigation technology specialists, as well as engage relevant stakeholders transparently, before deciding on the way forward," she said in a statement today.
Yeo said the proposed ban could affect more than six million road users who depend on real-time navigation.
She questioned why Gulf Cooperation Council nations had not banned Waze despite their proximity to the Middle East conflict and stringent national security measures.
She also asked whether the government had engaged Waze's parent company, United States-based Alphabet, to explore technical measures, including hosting Malaysian users' location data on local servers, to address data sovereignty concerns.
On alternatives, Yeo said motorists and commercial drivers often relied on multiple navigation applications to compare routes, road hazards and real-time traffic conditions.
"If the administration intends to replace Waze, what credible, enterprise-grade alternatives is the government currently evaluating, and have their operational capacity and routing algorithms been stress-tested for nationwide commercial use?" she said.
She also questioned whether the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) had the technical capacity to develop and maintain its TuJu navigation application to compete with established global platforms.
"A reactionary ban risks unnecessary public disruption, economic friction for the gig economy and reputational damage to Malaysia's digital landscape," she said.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had not ruled out a
complete ban on Waze
if suitable alternatives, including locally developed navigation applications, became available.
The announcement followed Wednesday's decision to
prohibit civil servants from using Waze
over national security and data protection concerns linked to the application's Israeli origins and legal jurisdiction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two men drown in river near Tanjung Rambutan
Article:
IPOH: Two men, aged 42 and 50, drowned at Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Tonggang in Tanjung Rambutan here today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 2.55pm requesting assistance to retrieve the victims.
He said firefighters from the Tambun Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 3.28pm and found police personnel at the scene.
"The men were found unconscious near the river, about 600 metres from the access point. Our personnel had to trek through the jungle to reach them," he said in a statement.
Firefighters retrieved the men using stretchers, with personnel wearing personal flotation devices during the operation.
The victims were carried across the river and handed over to Health Ministry personnel, who confirmed both had died. Their bodies were then handed over to the police for further action.
Eight firefighters, supported by a fire rescue tender and an emergency medical rescue services vehicle, took part in the operation, alongside five police personnel and six Health Ministry personnel.
The operation ended at 5.05pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: BN should not underestimate PN's strength, says Wawasan
Article:
KOTA BARU: Barisan Nasional (BN) should not underestimate Perikatan Nasional's (PN) strength in Melaka, as cooperation between the two coalitions could bolster their challenge against Pakatan Harapan (PH).
Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) information chief Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal said PN had a solid support base in the state and could help BN shore up its position in seats where it had faced narrow victories in the previous election.
"PN has strength in Melaka, and this should not be underestimated," he said.
Wan Ahmad Fayhsal said BN could also benefit from cooperation by easing pressure in the eight to 10 seats where its position was less secure in the previous state election.
On seat negotiations, the Machang MP said Wawasan was not seeking a large allocation and recognised Melaka as a BN stronghold.
"We understand that BN leads in Melaka, and we are willing to compromise for the sake of Muslim unity," he said.
He said Wawasan could help narrow the gap between BN and Pas, adding that several seats won by BN in the previous election had been decided by slim majorities of between 300 and 500 votes in three-cornered contests.
"Our strength could help narrow that gap," he said.
Commenting on PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan's statement that PN supporters had been asked to back BN candidates, while BN supporters could also support PN candidates, Wan Ahmad Fayhsal said Wawasan would extend similar support.
He said Wawasan had about 100,000 members nationwide, with at least 1,000 in each parliamentary constituency in Melaka.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen killed in crash had bought birthday gifts for sister
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 16-year-old boy who died when a family car skidded and crashed into a tree in Bagan here last night had bought birthday gifts for his younger sister just hours before the tragedy.
Putera Muhaimin Qudrat Mohd Noorwandi had bought the gifts during a family dinner outing in town, hoping to give them to his sister, Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis, 15, when they returned home.
His father, Mohd Noorwandi A Rahim, 41, said his son never got the chance to fulfil that wish.
"He bought several gifts for his sister's birthday, intending to hand them to her as soon as we reached home. Sadly, he never made it back," he said.
Noorwandi added that his son had shown exceptional generosity towards his mother, Norfarahin Mohammad, 38, just two days before his death.
Putera Muhaimin, a Form Four student at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Semerah, was buried at the Parit Bajuri Muslim cemetery here at 2pm today.
A sombre atmosphere hung over the cemetery as family members, relatives and close friends gathered to pay their last respects. His body had undergone a post-mortem at the forensic department of Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI), which was completed at 11.30am.
In the 10pm accident, the car carrying Putera Muhaimin and his family
skidded
off Jalan Johor Baru-Melaka before crashing into a tree.
Three of his siblings, aged 15, 11 and three, were injured, while his uncle, Nor Azlan Shaharudin, 27, who was driving, was seriously injured after being trapped in the driver's seat. He is receiving treatment at HSNI.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man dies buried in soil while hunting for gemstones
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 48-year-old man was killed after being buried under about one metre of soil while searching for gemstones near a water tank in Taman Kedidi, Pasir Gudang, today.
Jamaluddin Wahab, from Taman Cahaya, Masai, was searching for gemstones with a friend at Jalan Kedidi 26 when the soil collapsed on him.
His friend escaped unhurt and alerted the authorities.
Pasir Gudang Fire and Rescue Department station chief Firdaus Ahmad said a distress call was received at 10am. Seventeen rescuers from the Pasir Gudang and Johor Jaya stations were dispatched to the scene.
"The search and rescue operation was suspended at 11.46am due to heavy rain.
"The operation later resumed using specialised equipment, hoes and shovels," he said when contacted.
Firdaus said the victim was extricated at 12.33pm and pronounced dead by medical personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreigner arriving from Penang held in Hong Kong with 2kg of cocaine
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 25-year-old Chinese national arriving from Penang was arrested at Hong Kong International Airport last Thursday after 2kg of suspected cocaine were found in his checked-in luggage.
Hong Kong Customs said in a statement yesterday that the drugs were discovered during an inspection of his luggage.
The man was charged with trafficking in dangerous drugs, with the case scheduled to be mentioned at the West Kowloon magistrate's court today.
Hong Kong Customs said it would step up enforcement against cross-border drug trafficking through intelligence analysis.
It also reminded the public not to carry controlled goods or items of unknown contents for others, even in exchange for payment.
Under Hong Kong's Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, drug trafficking carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment and a fine of HK$5 million (RM2.7 million) upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SK Puchong Utama 2 team wins special award for RM114 pothole detector
Article:
SHAH ALAM: On a budget of just RM114, a team of five pupils from SK Puchong Utama 2 proved that cost is no barrier to high-impact innovation, clinching the Special Award in the Digital Innovation Category at the 2026 Selangor State Metamorphosis appreciation ceremony yesterday.
Known as Team Harmoni, the five Year Six pupils impressed the judges with their Pothole Detector On-The-Go, an Internet of Things (IoT)-based innovation that detects potholes in real time.
They earned a RM2,000 cash prize, a trophy, and a certificate of appreciation.
What makes the feat even more remarkable is that the team outperformed 240 other participants, including those from higher education institutions, local authorities, and government-linked and private companies, in a competition that showcased a range of high-impact innovations.
Team member Syafierul Qaleef Shahrul Anuar, 12, said the idea for the device arose from a concern for road user safety and was also inspired by the school syllabus he had been learning since July.
"It did not cost much. We built this project for about RM114 only. We used components like light-emitting diodes (LEDs), a buzzer, an ultrasonic sensor, a guard sensor, a toy car and many other parts.
"What we built is actually part of what we learn in school. Personally, I dream of studying engineering and building robots for agriculture and plantations," he said when met by Bernama at the Hilton Shah Alam, Glenmarie, last night.
The award was presented by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, accompanied by State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin and State Executive Councillor for Islamic Affairs and Innovation Culture, Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah.
Meanwhile, the team's accompanying teacher, Amirah Najihah Mohd Taufik, 25, explained that the Pothole Detector On-The-Go was designed specifically to spot road damage and send signals and alerts directly to a monitoring system.
"The device was actually created to detect potholes on the road. It sounds an alert to indicate a pothole, and we connect it directly to the system. The system transmits data in real time so that those monitoring it can pinpoint the exact location of the pothole.
"The system also comes with various other alert functions. The R&D for this project has been carried out since July by five pupils. They were selected based on the highest scores in Science and their excellent presentation skills," she said.
Amirah said the innovation is highly relevant, given that potholes are a critical problem that can cause accidents or injuries to road users.
She added that the device will be further developed with integrated cameras and AI technology, boosting its effectiveness and its potential for use both locally and abroad.
She added that the school is open to collaboration with any party to strengthen and expand the innovation.
An annual state government event, the 2026 Selangor State Metamorphosis Appreciation Ceremony recognises and celebrates excellence in innovation across the civil service, private sector, higher education institutions, schools and the public. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Forest fires: Over 22,500ha remains under response in Indonesia
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia is continuing firefighting operations across approximately 22,595ha of forest and land, with Central Kalimantan accounting for the largest affected area.
National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) acting head of data, information, and disaster communication centre Berton Panjaitan said the area still under response as of Oct 22 comprised 21,404ha in six priority provinces on Sumatra and Kalimantan islands, and another 1,243.70ha elsewhere, including Java, Sulawesi, and Maluku.
"In Kalimantan, the area still under response reached approximately 18,973ha comprising about 16,097ha in Central Kalimantan, 1,506ha in South Kalimantan, and 1,370ha in West Kalimantan.
"In Sumatra, the area still under response reached approximately 2,431ha comprising about 2,050ha in South Sumatra, 379ha in Jambi, and 2ha in Riau," he said in a statement.
Berton said a combined 71,878 personnel and 54 helicopters had been deployed to support firefighting operations in the six priority provinces comprising South Sumatra, Riau, and Jambi on Sumatra, and Central, South, and West Kalimantan on the Indonesian part of Borneo.
Earlier, Berton said Indonesia was assessing international assistance involving advanced equipment and technology unavailable domestically, while welcoming offers from other countries, state news agency Antara reported on Thursday.
Separately, the news agency reported that Indonesian police had registered 386 reports involving forest and land fire cases, including those linked to 22 corporations affiliated with foreign investments.
National Police Chief General Suyudi Ario Seto was quoted as saying that the reports comprised 286 cases involving individuals and 100 involving corporations, with 243 people and 13 corporations named suspects.
Police had recommended permit revocations in 23 corporate cases. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor schools to reopen on Monday as haze improves [WATCH]
Article:
JOHOR BARU: All schools in Johor will reopen on Monday following an improvement in the haze situation, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings declining across the state over the past five days.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made at a meeting of the Johor State Disaster Management Committee, based on assessments by relevant agencies.
He said changing wind directions, rising humidity and forecast rain were expected to help ease the haze, while health risk assessments by the Johor Health Department had been taken into account to safeguard pupils, teachers and school staff.
"The reopening is also important to ensure pupils can sit their year-end examinations and prepare for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination," he said in a statement today.
The Johor Education Department will coordinate compliance with existing safety and health standard operating procedures (SOPs), including the use of face masks and close monitoring of school activities based on current API readings and prevailing guidelines.
Naqib said the state government and relevant agencies would continue to monitor the situation, with any further measures announced through official channels.
He said the state remained committed to protecting the health and safety of school communities while ensuring that pupils' education was not disrupted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt targets 125,000 professional huffaz by 2050 - Zahid
Article:
MELAKA: The government is confident of producing 125,000 professional huffaz by 2050 by expanding access to technical higher education, strengthening Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and combining Quranic knowledge with professional and advanced technology skills.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the target builds on the National Transformation Programme 2050 (TN50) vision of developing a generation of huffaz who are not only proficient in Quranic memorisation but also capable of contributing to the country's strategic sectors.
He said about 12,500 professional huffaz had been produced so far, while opportunities for tahfiz and pondok school students to pursue higher education at Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) and six universities under the Malaysian Technical Universities Network (MTUN) would be expanded from 2027.
"We are confident that by providing tahfiz and pondok school students who have memorised the Quran with access to UniKL and the six MTUN universities, we can achieve the target of producing 125,000 professional huffaz by 2050," he told reporters after a huffaz graduation and Ulul Albab excellence appreciation ceremony today.
Zahid said clearer pathways into technical and professional higher education would enable huffaz to acquire specialised skills and professional qualifications to meet the country's future workforce needs.
Earlier, Zahid, who is also National TVET Council chairman, said tahfiz students should have clear educational pathways from school to higher education, TVET and professional careers, allowing them to pursue fields suited to their interests and abilities.
"We do not want tahfiz students to feel that they have only one path in life. Their mastery of the Quran can instead serve as a foundation for pursuing various fields according to their interests and abilities," he said.
He said the initiative was also being strengthened through Tahfiz TVET and TVET Tahfiz programmes involving institutions under Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara), GiatMara, UniKL and industry partners to expand training and employment opportunities.
He encouraged tahfiz students to explore artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, the digital economy and advanced technology, not merely as users but also as creators capable of developing solutions to real-world problems.
Zahid said tahfiz education should go beyond Quranic memorisation by giving students opportunities to develop their academic, technical, leadership and professional capabilities while preserving their religious values and identity.
He also expressed his aspiration for Malaysia to one day be led by a prime minister who is an al-Hafiz or al-Hafizah and possesses the knowledge, integrity and ability to govern the country. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian aid to Yemen - Mohamad
Article:
SEREMBAN: Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian assistance to Yemen, while urging all parties in the protracted conflict in the country to return to the negotiation table and look for a diplomatic solution.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia empathises with the suffering of the Yemeni people who have to endure the effects of the protracted civil war, including famine and hardship in getting basic necessities.
He said the matter was brought up by his counterpart, Yemen's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, who shared on the latest developments in the country via a phone call on Thursday.
"Malaysia stands ready to participate in any relief mission or deliver assistance to countries that require it, to the best of our ability," he told reporters after handing over Deepavali festive contributions at the Rantau community hall today.
Mohamad said the conflict must be brought to an end as it brings no benefit to the estimated 22 million affected inhabitants and instead inflicts prolonged suffering.
In light of this, he urged foreign stakeholders to play a constructive role by returning to negotiation table to bring peace and prosperity to the people of Yemen.
He said diplomatic efforts need to be prioritised in order to prevent the conflict from dragging on and undermining regional stability. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police tracking down trio after men filmed riding atop moving Proton Wira
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police are tracking down the owner, driver and passengers of a blue Proton Wira after two men were filmed sitting on its roof as it moved along a road in Taman Puteri Wangsa, Ulu Tiram.
Johor Baru Selatan district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said police detected the video and photographs at 9am today.
He said the car was seen travelling from Jalan Beladau 32 towards Jalan Bukit Jaya.
"Investigations are ongoing to identify the individuals involved," he said in a statement.
The case is being investigated under Section 47 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for carrying a person outside a vehicle or in a manner that could interfere with the driver's control and endanger other road users.
Those with information can contact the Johor Baru Selatan Traffic Police Station at 07-223 7977.
The New Straits Times reported yesterday that two men were filmed sitting on the roof of the
moving Proton Wira
while a third person drove the car.
The footage, believed to have been recorded by a motorist travelling behind the vehicle, showed the men appearing unfazed as the car continued along the road.
At one point, the Wira slowed down near a speed breaker, leaving the men struggling to maintain their balance.
The person recording the video was heard reading out the vehicle's registration number and mentioning the location where the incident allegedly occurred.
The video was later shared on Facebook, garnering more than 20,000 views and over 200 comments, with many users condemning the stunt and questioning why anyone would risk their lives and those of other road users.
Police have identified Taman Puteri Wangsa, Ulu Tiram, as the location linked to the incident and are working to identify those involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysian company linked to ketamine-laden tanker seized in Indonesia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A tanker seized by Indonesian authorities over the suspected smuggling of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine has been traced to a company registered in Malaysia.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the MT Global 168 was owned by a Johor Baru-based company with two Malaysian directors in their 40s and 50s.
He said both directors had no previous criminal records and would be called in to assist investigations.
"The vessel is registered under a company with two Malaysian directors, both in their 40s and 50s. Neither has any previous criminal record, and we will summon them to assist in our investigations," he told reporters here today.
Hussein said the vessel had previously applied to be registered under the Malaysian flag, but the process had not been completed.
"The tanker is currently sailing under the Mongolian flag," he said.
Earlier, Hussein said Malaysian police would seek
further information
from the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) following the seizure of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine hydrochloride from the tanker, which had travelled through Malaysian waters.
The vessel was believed to have made unusual movements between Oct 14 and 18 before being intercepted off Tanjung Balai Asahan, Indonesia.
Investigations indicated that it had departed from an anchorage in Pasir Gudang, Johor, stopped at Port Klang to refuel, then headed towards the Andaman Sea.
The crew reportedly switched off the vessel's Automatic Identification System (AIS) for three days to evade detection.
Eight crew members – seven Indonesians and a Chinese national – were detained on Tuesday in connection with the seizure.
Indonesian National Police chief General Suyudi Ario Seto was reported as saying that authorities had been monitoring the vessel since August after receiving intelligence about suspicious activities.
The seizure has prompted further investigations into the vessel's Malaysian ownership and movements before it was intercepted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two Malaysians injured by Typhoon Champi in stable condition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two Malaysians who sustained minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi in Taiwan are receiving
treatment at separate hospitals
and their conditions are reported to be stable.
Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC) President Bong Yik Jui said the victims, both 57, were receiving treatment at Dali Jen Ai Hospital in Taichung and Miaoli Daqian Hospital in Miaoli, respectively.
"We contacted them separately and confirmed that they are in stable condition," he told Bernama.
He added that one of the Malaysians had been discharged from hospital after receiving treatment.
Bong said the MFTC would closely monitor developments related to Typhoon Champi, particularly its implications for the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan.
"MFTC will remain in contact with the Malaysian community through existing communication channels," he said.
Media reported that Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, leaving one
dead and more than 500 injured.
The typhoon also damaged hundreds of buildings, disrupted electricity supply, and forced flight cancellations.
As of August, this year, there were 34,833 Malaysians in Taiwan, including 7,615 students.
Bong urged Malaysians residing in or visiting Taiwan to monitor local weather advisories and adhere to safety instrutions and evacuation orders issued by local authorities.
Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information concerning other Malaysian nationals who may require assistance in the affected areas, are urged to contact MFTC in Taipei at +886 972 349 343 or via email at mwtaipei@kln.gov.my.
Bong also urged Malaysians in Taiwan to register and regularly update their contact details through the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my (https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my/) to facilitate timely communication and consular assistance, particularly during emergencies.
He also encouraged Malaysians to follow the MFTC's social media channels for the latest updates and advisories.
The MFTC serves as Malaysia's official representative office in Taipei, performing consular functions similar to those of Malaysian diplomatic and consular missions abroad and providing assistance and support to Malaysians in Taiwan. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan education dept probing claims students served alcohol at dinner
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Education Department is finalising an investigation regarding allegations of students from a school being involved in the serving of alcoholic beverages during a dinner event held by the school's alumni association on Sept 5.
In a statement today, the department said that school students should not be involved in activities involving the handling or serving of alcoholic beverages.
Based on initial information, the event was organised by the alumni association outside the school premises, while the school and the association denied allegations of student involvement in the serving of
alcoholic beverages
, it said.
The department said that the investigation into complaints received through the Public Complaint Management System (SISPAA) also includes an examination of the school's compliance with procedures.
"If there are any violations of regulations or negligence in the performance of duties, appropriate action will be taken based on the applicable regulations," read the statement.
The department emphasised that the welfare, safety, and dignity of students are always a priority and that it (the department) will ensure that the investigation results are thoroughly reviewed before any follow-up actions are taken.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning in 9 states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 6pm today.
The warning covers Perlis, Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak), as well as Langkawi and Kubang Pasu in Kedah.
The warning also applies to Kota Tinggi and Johor Baru in Johor; Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus and Setiu in Terengganu; and Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas and Tumpat in Kelantan.
In Sabah, the affected areas are Kudat; Sandakan; Tawau (Tawau, Kunak and Semporna); the West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang and Tuaran); and the Interior (Tambunan, Sook, Keningau, Beaufort, Tenom, Sipitang and Pensiangan).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Bintulu (Tatau and Sebauh); Kapit (Kapit and Belaga); Limbang; Miri (Marudi, Bario, Beluru and Telang Usan); and Sibu (Selangau). — BERNAMA

Title: PM: Govt prepared to absorb fuel subsidy cost of up to RM45b a year
Article:
Bernama
MELAKA: The government is prepared to absorb an increase in fuel subsidy costs, which could reach RM45 billion annually amid a surge in global crude oil prices, rather than pass the burden on to the people through higher fuel prices.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government remained committed to maintaining the price of RON95 petrol at RM1.99 per litre despite international crude oil prices climbing to between US$120 and US$130 a barrel.
He said the move was aimed at shielding the public, particularly low- and middle-income groups, from the impact of rising global fuel prices and the resulting pressure on household expenses.
"If oil prices continue to surge, the cost borne by the government could reach between RM42 billion and RM45 billion a year. If we raise fuel prices in line with market rates, people would have to pay an additional RM2 or RM3, or at least RM5 a day.
"Imagine those who have to send their children to school and go to work themselves. That could mean an extra RM10 a day. It is better for the government to bear the burden than to burden the people, our parents," he said at the 'Sentuhan Kasih Madani' Programme and the launch of the National Cost of Living Action Plan 2030 at the Hang Jebat Sports Complex in Krubong.
Anwar said global crude oil prices had nearly doubled from around US$70 a barrel previously, putting many countries under mounting cost-of-living pressures.
However, he said the government had chosen to continue absorbing a substantial portion of fuel subsidy costs to prevent consumers from facing steep petrol price increases if prices were allowed to float in line with market rates.
He also rejected the view that generous subsidies made the people overly dependent on government assistance, stressing that policies must take into account the realities faced by low-income households.
Anwar said the government would continue to balance efforts to drive economic growth with its responsibility to ensure that national progress translated into a better standard of living and greater well-being for the people.
He said the country's economic success should not be measured solely by growth, investment and trade, but also by the tangible benefits it delivered in improving the people's standard of living and well-being.
He said efforts to drive economic growth, including through mastery of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductors, must go hand in hand with addressing the people's basic needs, particularly the cost of living, education, healthcare and employment opportunities.
"We are not talking merely about figures and statistics, but about people.
"The government's approach is guided by the principle of 'reaching for the sky while remaining rooted in the ground', which requires the country to continue exploring new fields of knowledge and technology without neglecting human values, ethics, culture and the well-being of the people at the grassroots level," he said.
Also present were Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali and his deputy, Datuk Fuziah Salleh. — BERNAMA

Title: Melaka polls: Damian Yeo would quit politics rather than give Bemban to Bersatu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Melaka DAP chairman Damian Yeo has vowed to quit politics rather than accept any move by Pakatan Harapan (PH) to cede the Bemban state seat to Bersatu in the upcoming Melaka election.
The former Duyong assemblyman said he learnt of the possibility while discussing candidates, campaign strategies and the political landscape with another former Melaka DAP chairman.
"But when I heard that the plan under PH Plus could involve giving up Bemban to Bersatu, my immediate reaction was... Forget it, I am out," he said in a Facebook post.
Yeo said the wounds of past political betrayals remained fresh, making it difficult for him to accept any proposed cooperation with Bersatu.
"The wound from being stabbed in the back is still fresh. Some political betrayals are simply too difficult to forget, let alone forgive.
"I have been there, done that, and paid the price," he said.
He said he had decided to withdraw from political activities, including campaigning in the Melaka election.
His remarks come amid speculation over a possible electoral arrangement between PH and Bersatu.
On Sept 19, Melaka PH chairman
Datuk Seri Adly Zahari confirmed
that discussions were being held with Bersatu on a possible PH Plus collaboration.
However, Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said on Wednesday that PH would contest the state election on its own, without cooperating with other parties, including Bersatu.
He also said DAP intended to contest eight seats, including Bemban, which its former chairman Datuk Tey Kok Kiew lost in the 2021 state election.

Title: Worker killed, another injured in suspected drink-driving crash in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 28-year-old worker was killed when a drunk driver rammed his car into him while he was installing warning signs along Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar early today.
City police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 26-year-old driver recorded an alcohol breath screening reading of 64mg/100ml and was arrested and remanded for three days until Monday to assist in investigations.
He said the accident occurred at about 5am when the car, travelling from Jalan Damansara towards Jalan Parlimen, lost control and struck two workers in the left lane.
"The victim, a supervisor, was pronounced dead while receiving treatment, while another worker, a 49-year-old lorry driver, sustained injuries to his head and right hand. The lorry driver is receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital. The car driver escaped uninjured.
"The five workers, comprising a supervisor, a lorry driver and three Bangladeshi workers, had been carrying out warning sign installation works under a Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) contract.
"The work began at 11pm on Oct 23 and ended at 4am today," he said in a statement.
Zamzuri said the case was being investigated under Sections 44(1)(b) and 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Section 44 of the Act covers offences involving driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs that causes death.
Those with information about the incident are urged to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.

Title: 251 sexual offence cases involving tertiary students reported in 8 months
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 251 sexual offence cases involving higher education students were reported between January and August this year.
Citing police statistics, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said the figures underscored the need for sustained efforts to improve sexual safety in educational institutions.
She said the Waja Siswa Squad, part of the Women Against Crime initiative, was established to promote volunteerism and community involvement in raising awareness and addressing violence against women.
"In tackling this issue, we must not only understand how to protect ourselves but also how to help others appropriately," she said when officiating the Melaka-level Waja Siswa Squad programme at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) here today.
Also present were the ministry's deputy secretary-general (Management) Datuk Ruziah Shafei and Women's Development Department director-general Hanani Sapit.
Lim said violence against women and sexual harassment should not be taken lightly, as they could take various forms, including threats, humiliation, emotional manipulation, financial control and sexual abuse.
She said actions dismissed as jokes or expressions of affection should not be normalised if they violated personal boundaries, caused fear or made someone feel threatened.
She urged students to understand their rights and learn how to seek help if they experienced sexual harassment.
Lim also called on UTeM students, regardless of gender, to raise awareness among their peers and help create a campus environment that rejects violence and promotes healthy relationships.
She said the programme was expected to strengthen student participation in efforts to make campuses safer.
Lim said 340,667 volunteers had joined the Waja Squad nationwide as of September, comprising 264,461 women and 76,206 men.
She said men's participation as allies was important in promoting respect for women, rejecting harassment and encouraging healthy relationships, stressing that preventing violence was not solely women's responsibility.

Title: Terengganu govt extends condolences over Tengku Baderul Zaman's passing
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu state government has extended its condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire royal family following the passing of Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah today.
The condolences were conveyed by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, who also expressed them on behalf of the people of Terengganu in a statement on his Facebook page.
"May Allah SWT forgive all the late Tengku Baderul Zaman's sins, shower His mercy upon him, accept his good deeds and place his soul among His faithful and righteous servants.
"May all members of the family and the royal household be granted fortitude and strength in facing this loss," he said.
Samsuri said the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, had decreed a three-day mourning period beginning today.
"The people of Terengganu are requested to respect the mourning period and comply with the stipulated rules, including the dress code when paying their last respects to the late Tengku Baderul Zaman," he said.
Tengku Baderul Zaman, the younger brother of Sultan Mizan,
died at 1.20am today at Gleneagles Hospital
in Kuala Lumpur.

Title: Sabah Pan Borneo 95pct complete, contractors given until year-end
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Contractors handling three critical work packages of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project along the Putatan, Penampang, Inanam, Sepanggar and Tuaran stretches have been instructed to complete the remaining construction works by the end of this year.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said completing the three packages was crucial to improving traffic flow around Kota Kinabalu and reducing congestion on existing routes.
He said Work Packages 6 (WP06), 7 (WP07) and 8 (WP08) were nearing completion but could not yet be fully opened as several sections were still under construction.
"I have personally asked for construction works along these stretches to be completed by the end of this year. They must be completed by year-end. Once the Pan Borneo Highway is completed, traffic flow can be improved.
"This means vehicles that do not need to stop in Kota Kinabalu, particularly those heading directly to Beaufort and Papar, can use this route.
"So far, I have been informed that construction is 95 per cent complete, with only a few sections remaining. We will monitor the progress and ensure it is completed by the end of this year," he said after launching the Madani Kita @ Sepanggar programme in Manggatal, near today.
Mustapha, who is also Sepanggar member of parliament, was responding to questions about measures to address delays in the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, particularly along the stretches passing through his constituency.
The three packages comprise WP06 from Putatan to Inanam, WP07 from Inanam to Sepanggar, and WP08 from Sepanggar to Berungis Roundabout.
They are key components of the Kota Kinabalu Outer Ring Road, which is designed to divert some traffic away from the city centre.
Mustapha acknowledged that all three packages had been delayed and were considered critical because they involved urban routes that frequently experience congestion.
"We hope this stretch of the Pan Borneo Highway will be completed by the end of the year so that congestion on existing routes can be eased," he said.
Commenting on traffic congestion in Sepanggar, particularly before motorists enter the Pan Borneo Highway stretch near Kampung Tebobon, Mustapha said the problem stemmed from the concentration of traffic on existing roads, which were also used by heavy vehicles.
He said this had caused several sections of the road to deteriorate frequently, especially during rainy weather. The damage continued to recur despite repair works because of the weak road structure and constant use.
"The road damage is repaired, but the problem now is that the repairs do not last because the road is used daily.
"We have asked the Public Works Department (PWD) and the contractors to ensure the road is safe for users," he said.
Phase 1 of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project comprises 35 work packages spanning 706km.
The Auditor-General's Report 2/2026 stated that
only four of the 35 packages, or 11.4 per cent,
had been fully completed as at March 31, while the remaining 31 were still under implementation.
However, the figures refer to the number of packages fully completed, rather than the overall physical progress of the project.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister and state Works and Utilities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam had earlier said physical progress under Phase 1A had reached 89.54 per cent as at Sept 25, compared with the scheduled progress of 96.23 per cent.
In a separate development, Mustapha said the Madani Kita @ Sepanggar programme was organised by the Sabah Federal Youth and Sports Department, with young people making up about 80 per cent of its participants.

Title: Sultan Sharafuddin wants no Selangor resident left behind amid state's progress
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Despite Selangor's status as one of Malaysia's most developed states, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah remains concerned about subjects, particularly the poor and underprivileged, who continue to struggle with daily life.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said the Sultan's role as Head of the Islamic Religion in Selangor extended beyond safeguarding the faith and strengthening religious institutions to protecting the Muslim community's welfare while maintaining harmony with non-Muslims.
Salehuddin, who has known the Sultan for nearly 18 years and is a member of the Selangor Royal Council, said the ruler took his responsibility to safeguard his subjects' welfare, uphold the sanctity of Islam and ensure justice seriously.
"His Highness is always deeply concerned about matters affecting the Muslim community. Should there be instances where Muslims are oppressed, left without economic support or struck by misfortune, His Highness is the first to instruct us, the religious institutions, to take action," he told Bernama in an interview held in conjunction with the recent Silver Jubilee celebration of the Sultan's reign.
Salehuddin said the Sultan paid particular attention to low-income Muslims and those living in poverty, insisting that they be identified so assistance could reach them effectively.
"In every discussion, His Highness consistently reminds us that the poor and destitute must not be sidelined. He emphasises the need to compile data so that this group continues to receive the attention it needs," he said.
Despite his pride in Selangor's development, Sultan Sharafuddin has cautioned against measuring the state's success solely in economic terms while some of its people remain poor.
Salehuddin said the Sultan was aware of urban poverty, including residents of dilapidated flats where large families were forced to live in cramped two-room homes.
The Sultan has questioned the value of celebrating the state's progress if sections of society remain marginalised.
In response, he has directed religious institutions, including the Selangor Zakat Board, to identify asnaf, or zakat-eligible recipients, and ensure assistance reaches those who need it most.
Salehuddin said the Sultan had also said that state policies and budget allocations must address the housing, education and daily needs of underprivileged communities.
On strengthening Islam, Salehuddin said the Sultan wanted Muslims' aqidah (faith) preserved in accordance with the Ahli Sunnah wal Jamaah tradition, while measures were taken to curb deviant teachings and ideologies such as liberalism and pluralism.
He said religious institutions, including mosques and surau, must be managed professionally, particularly in administration and finance, to maintain public confidence.
The Sultan also wanted comprehensive religious programmes to reach urban and rural communities, including the B40 and other underprivileged groups, so that the benefits of development and welfare were shared more equitably.
At the same time, efforts to strengthen Islam must go hand in hand with respect for other religions to preserve social harmony.
Salehuddin said the Sultan viewed unity among Muslims and positive relations among people of different ethnic backgrounds and faiths as essential to national development.
Community leaders, he said, should promote unity rather than deepen divisions.
"His Highness expects community leaders never to act as the masterminds behind societal fragmentation. Instead, they should encourage Muslims and people of other ethnic groups to live in harmony and unity," he said.
The younger generation is another priority for the Sultan, who has repeatedly reminded Mais and the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) not to overlook young people when planning religious programmes at state, district, mosque and surau levels.
Salehuddin said Sultan Sharafuddin wanted targeted initiatives to draw young people to mosques and surau through activities suited to their interests, including sports and recreation after the Subuh (dawn) prayer.
Mosque and surau committees had also been urged to engage younger congregants and diversify activities to make religious institutions more welcoming.
"We must not focus solely on the adult or older generations when planning initiatives to enliven our mosques," he said.
Salehuddin said the Sultan had called on mosque and surau committees to move beyond conventional approaches and tailor programmes to different segments of society.
Through such efforts, mosques and surau could serve not only as places of worship but also as centres for learning, strengthening community ties, distributing aid and bringing young people closer to religion.
Ultimately, the Sultan's vision for the Muslim community extends beyond economic growth and strong religious institutions to caring for the poor, preserving social harmony and ensuring no one is left behind.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar extends condolences to Terengganu Sultan over brother's passing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, on the passing of His Royal Highness's younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.

Article:

Title: Melaka polls: Wawasan wants to contest under PN logo, says Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) wants to contest the Melaka election under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) logo.
Its president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the party preferred to use the coalition's logo, but would discuss alternatives if necessary.
"If possible, we want to use the PN logo. If not, we will have to sit down again as a team and decide which logo is best for us," he told reporters.
Hamzah said
PN had initiated legal action
after receiving a notice from the Registrar of Societies (RoS) suspending and subsequently deregistering the coalition on Oct 20.
"When we received the letter from the RoS, we took it to court as quickly as possible.
"That shows we believe the PN logo represents all of us, and that it is our team," he said.
On Oct 22, the High Court
granted PN a stay
against the RoS action pending the full disposal of its judicial
review, without ruling on the legality of the deregistration.
The ruling allows PN to continue its political activities while the legal challenge is pending.
PN election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor welcomed the decision, saying it would
allow the coalition to continue operating
pending the judicial review.
Sanusi had earlier said PN was prepared to contest the Melaka polls under the Pas moon logo if it could not use its own.
