Title: Anwar chairs three major PKR meetings in Melaka before campaign launch
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 24 — Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended three key party meetings held at around 3 pm today.
The three important meetings, held at a hotel in Banda Hilir, comprised the State Leadership Council (MPN) meeting, the Central Political Bureau meeting and the PKR Central Leadership Council (MPP) meeting.
The strategic meetings reportedly involved the participation of nearly 40 party leaders.
Among the top party leaders who also attended the meetings were acting deputy president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh, Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim and Melaka Leadership Council chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim.
Anwar is also scheduled to attend the announcement of candidates and the launch of the Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) election machinery at Stadium Hang Jebat in Krubong at around 8 pm today.
The 16th Melaka state election is scheduled to be held on Nov 14, with nomination day set for Oct 31 and early voting on November 10. — Bernama

Title: Two men found dead by riverbank after swimming in Sungai Tonggang
Article:
IPOH, Oct 24 — Two men were found dead by a riverbank after swimming in a river, near Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Tonggang, Tanjung Rambutan, here today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident involving two victims, aged 42 and 50, at 2.55 pm.
Upon arriving at the location, the firefighters had to walk along a 600-metre jungle trekking path to reach both victims who were found unconscious by the riverbank.
“The rescue team then brought both victims out from across the river before the Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers confirmed their deaths at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
He said the bodies of both victims were handed over to the police for further action. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu Sultan’s younger brother laid to rest
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 24 —The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, was laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum of Masjid Al-Muktafi Billah Shah here today.
The funeral rites for Tengku Baderul Zaman, who died at the age of 52, were completed at 6.10 pm.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, attended the funeral rites.
Also in attendance was Pahang’s Tengku Ampuan, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, accompanied by her children, to convey their condolences to the Terengganu royal family.
Also present was Terengganu State Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Mohd Nor Hamzah, together with the state government leadership.
Earlier, the late Tengku Baderul Zaman’s remains arrived at Sultan Mahmud Airport in Kuala Nerus at 1.20 pm today on a special aircraft before being taken to Balai Islam at Istana Syarqiyyah here at 2 pm to allow mourners to pay their last respects.
After funeral prayers at Balai Islam, the remains were taken to the Royal Mausoleum, arriving at 5.03 pm.
Terengganu Mufti Prof Dr Syed Hadzrullathfi Syed Omar led the recitation of Surah Yasin, followed by tahlil and prayers.
Tengku Baderul Zaman died at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital in Kuala Lumpur. He leaves behind his widow, Toh Puan Seri Wan Hidayah Wan Ismail, and three children. — Bernama

Title: Selangor Sultan graces Royal Tea Reception in conjunction with Silver Jubilee celebration
Article:
KLANG, Oct 24 —The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today graced a Royal Tea Reception attended by 1,500 retirees, investors and civil servants in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration of his reign at Istana Alam Shah here.
Also in attendance were the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, and the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah.
Upon arrival, their Royal Highnesses were received by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, and State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin.
The Royal Tea Reception was the final of five events organised to mark the celebration.
At the event, Sultan Sharafuddin also launched the ‘Lakaran Indah Institusi Setiausaha Kerajaan Negeri Selangor’ book.
Meanwhile, Selangor Public Service Commission chairman Datuk Haris Kasim, in his address, said Nov 22, 2001 was a historic date as it was the day Sultan Sharafuddin was proclaimed the ninth Sultan of Selangor.
“Over the past 25 years, Selangor has continued to progress as a dynamic, prosperous and competitive state, with Your Royal Highness remaining the guardian of the state’s sovereignty, a symbol of unity among the people and a pillar of stability for the Selangor Sultanate.
“Your Royal Highness’s decrees, advice and views on upholding the sanctity of Islam, harmony among the multiracial community and the well-being of the people have always served as a guiding principle for the state administration,” he said.
He said the strength of the civil service depended greatly on the quality, competence and integrity of its human capital. He therefore reminded himself and the Selangor civil servants to take the Sultan’s decrees and advice as a guide in discharging their responsibilities to the state and its people.
“An outstanding civil servant is not judged solely by efficiency in carrying out duties, but also by their character, honesty in upholding the trust placed in them, courtesy in delivering services and dedication to safeguarding the people’s interests,” he said.
Haris said Sultan Sharafuddin has a special place in the hearts of the state’s civil servants because the Sultan had served in the public sector before ascending the throne.
“His Royal Highness had served at the Selangor State Secretary’s Office, the Kuala Lumpur District Office and the Royal Malaysia Police in Kuala Lumpur, giving him first-hand exposure to the intricacies of government administration and the responsibilities involved in serving the people.
“His Royal Highness’s emphasis on integrity, efficiency, discipline and good governance reflects the values shaped by his experience in the civil service,” he said.
On the launch of ‘
Lakaran Indah Institusi Setiausaha Kerajaan Negeri Selangor
’, Haris said the book was an important effort to document history, trace the development of the state administration and record the contributions of 32 individuals who had served as State Secretary across different eras and amid various state development challenges.
“This book not only chronicles the leadership of those who came before us, but also serves as a tribute to their service, sacrifices and legacy of excellence in the state administration. It also enriches our repository of knowledge and provides guidance for future generations of civil servants,” he said.
He said the book is expected to inspire current generations of state administrators to remember the contributions of their predecessors and carry forward their legacy of dedicated public service under the reign of Sultan Sharafuddin. — Bernama

Title: Public urged to stay calm during RTS Link security exercise on Oct 27
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 24 —The RTS Link Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Exercise Field Training Exercise (FTX) 2026 will be held at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar Station and Wadi Hana Depot in Johor Bahru on Tuesday (Oct 27).
The National Security Council (MKN), Prime Minister’s Department, said the exercise would run from 9 am to 5 pm and be conducted in collaboration with Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd (MRTS Corp) and RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO).
In a statement today, MKN said the exercise aimed to test and assess preparedness, response capabilities and coordination among Malaysian and Singaporean security agencies and emergency services.
“It is being held ahead of the full operation of the RTS Link and will also test the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for cross-border incident management, jointly developed by Malaysia and Singapore,” MKN said.
The public has been advised to remain calm if they see security personnel, operational assets or exercise activities during the simulation.
MKN said there was no actual threat and all activities were simulations conducted solely for the exercise. — Bernama

Title: Home Ministry leaves decision on charged AKPS chief to civil service process
Article:
KULAI, Oct 24 — Matters concerning the position of Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will be handled by the Home Ministry secretary-general and the Chief Secretary to the Government, said Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the matter was being handled by the two officials in accordance with existing public administration regulations.
“The matter is being handled between my secretary-general and the Chief Secretary to the Government.
“This is because the public administration has regulations to deal with such situations,” he told a press conference after launching the 78th National Registration Day (HPN) celebration, the MADANI Adopted Village (KAM) and MADANI Adopted School (SAM) programmes here today.
He was responding to questions on Mohd Shuhaily’s position as AKPS director-general while facing a court case.
Responding to criticism from opposition MPs who claimed that he had failed to act as a mediator in the issue involving AKPS and its personnel, Saifuddin said he accepted the criticism with an open mind.
However, he also questioned the ability of opposition leaders to play the role of peacemakers when their own party was facing divisions, including a conflict between groups supporting Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
Last Wednesday, Mohd Shuhaily pleaded not guilty at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court to two charges of intentionally causing injuries to police personnel Faiz Saman and Ekmal Sofwan Dirman at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on Sept 28.
On the same day, lawyer Datuk Rosal Azimin Ahmad, who is representing Mohd Shuhaily, was reported as saying that his client would continue performing his duties as usual unless there was an administrative directive to the contrary, despite facing the two charges in court. — Bernama

Title: DAP’s Yeo warns nationwide Waze ban could disrupt logistics and gig economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — DAP national publicity secretary Yeo Bee Yin has cautioned the federal government against rushing into a blanket nationwide ban on the Waze navigation application, warning that a sudden prohibition would disrupt daily commutes, logistics, and gig-economy livelihoods for more than six million active Malaysian motorists.
The Puchong MP expressed serious concern over remarks by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who announced yesterday that Putrajaya has not ruled out a total ban once viable domestic alternatives mature.
“A policy decision of this scale must not be made in haste or taken lightly. It directly impacts over six million active Malaysian road users who depend on real-time navigation daily for their livelihoods, commutes, and logistics,” she said in a statement.
The prime minister's comments followed a circular issued on Wednesday barring all civil servants from using Waze over fears that official logistics and personal movement data could be harvested by the Israeli regime. Waze has dismissed the data security allegations as "completely false", asserting that its global operations adhere to strict international privacy standards.
While Anwar took to Facebook yesterday to apologise for public inconvenience, he maintained that national security cannot be compromised. He also urged motorists to exercise patience with the government's homegrown alternative, Tuju, which the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) and its private developer are currently refining.
Today, Yeo argued that before contemplating a nationwide blackout, Putrajaya must address critical technical and geopolitical inconsistencies.
On regional security, she questioned why Gulf Cooperation Council states, including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Qatar, and Kuwait, continue to permit Waze despite being situated adjacent to the conflict zone while enforcing stringent national security laws.
Addressing data sovereignty, Yeo asked whether the government had explored technical ring-fencing through direct, high-level discussions with Waze's US parent company, Alphabet. She noted that Putrajaya could negotiate to mandate local data residency, ensuring Malaysian telemetry and location records are hosted securely on sovereign domestic servers.
Yeo also cast doubt on whether a statutory regulator like LLM can build and maintain a crowd-sourced navigation engine capable of matching global technology firms. Real-time dynamic routing and low-latency road hazard updates, she said, require immense computing scale, continuous algorithmic refinement, and specialized software engineering.
She pointed to South Korea as a cautionary precedent. While Seoul restricts foreign mapping platforms under its Geospatial Information Management Act, its domestic navigation leaders, Naver Map and KakaoMap, were built and scaled by multi-billion-dollar private tech corporations rather than government agencies.
“All in all, a reactionary ban risks unnecessary public disruption, economic friction for the gig economy, and reputational damage to Malaysia’s digital landscape,” she said.
“We urge the National Security Council (MKN) to consult industry experts and navigation technology specialists as well as engage relevant stakeholders transparently before deciding on the way forward.”

Title: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain, strong winds in nine states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 6 pm today.
The warning covers Perlis, Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak), as well as Langkawi and Kubang Pasu in Kedah.
The warning also applies to Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru in Johor; Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus and Setiu in Terengganu; and Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas and Tumpat in Kelantan.
In Sabah, the affected areas are Kudat; Sandakan; Tawau (Tawau, Kunak and Semporna); the West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang and Tuaran); and the Interior (Tambunan, Sook, Keningau, Beaufort, Tenom, Sipitang and Pensiangan).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Bintulu (Tatau and Sebauh); Kapit (Kapit and Belaga); Limbang; Miri (Marudi, Bario, Beluru and Telang Usan); and Sibu (Selangau). — Bernama

Title: Two Malaysians injured in Typhoon Champi recovering in Taiwan hospitals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals who sustained minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi in Taiwan are receiving treatment at separate hospitals and their conditions are reported to be stable.
Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC) President Bong Yik Jui said the two, both 57, were receiving treatment at Dali Jen Ai Hospital in Taichung and Miaoli Daqian Hospital in Miaoli, respectively.
“We contacted both individuals separately and confirmed that they are in stable condition,” he told Bernama.
He added that one of the Malaysians had been discharged from hospital after receiving treatment.
Bong said the MFTC would closely monitor developments related to Typhoon Champi, particularly its implications for the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan.
“MFTC will remain in contact with the Malaysian community through existing communication channels,” he said.
Media reported that Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, leaving one dead and more than 500 injured. The typhoon also damaged hundreds of buildings, disrupted electricity supply, and forced flight cancellations.
As of August, this year, there were 34,833 Malaysians in Taiwan, including 7,615 students.
Bong urged Malaysians residing in or visiting Taiwan to monitor local weather advisories and adhere to safety instrutions and evacuation orders issued by local authorities.
Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information concerning other Malaysian nationals who may require assistance in the affected areas, are urged to contact MFTC in Taipei at +886 972 349 343 or via email at
mwtaipei@kln.gov.my
.
Bong also urged Malaysians in Taiwan to register and regularly update their contact details through the e-Konsular portal at
https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my
to facilitate timely communication and consular assistance, particularly during emergencies.
He also encouraged Malaysians to follow the MFTC’s social media channels for the latest updates and advisories.
The MFTC serves as Malaysia’s official representative office in Taipei, performing consular functions similar to those of Malaysian diplomatic and consular missions abroad and providing assistance and support to Malaysians in Taiwan. — Bernama

Title: Haze spreads to five Sarawak spots while Klang Valley air improves slightly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Air quality deteriorated further this afternoon, with 23 monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings on the Air Pollutant Index (API) at 4.00pm, up from 21 in the morning, according to the Department of Environment (DOE).
Of the 68 stations nationwide, 23 registered readings in the unhealthy range of 101 to 200, while 39 recorded moderate air quality and six remained in the good tier. No station entered very unhealthy or hazardous territory.
Seremban in Negeri Sembilan logged the worst air quality in the country at 172, up from 169 at 10.00am. Elsewhere in the state, Nilai recorded 166, while Port Dickson improved to 140. Melaka saw all three of its monitoring stations remain in the unhealthy tier, led by Bukit Rambai at 163, Bandaraya Melaka at 160, and Alor Gajah at 158.
Johor remained the worst-affected state, with eight stations in the unhealthy bracket after Kota Tinggi joined the list at 151. Batu Pahat and Kluang climbed to 166 and 165 respectively, with Kluang matching Larkin, which eased to 165 from 169. Tangkak registered 162, Pasir Gudang 161, Segamat 155, and Pengerang 154.
In East Malaysia, Sarawak saw the sharpest rise in affected areas, expanding from three to five unhealthy stations. IPD Serian rose to 160, Sri Aman to 157, and Kapit to 153, while Kuching and Samarahan entered the bracket at 155 and 153. In Pahang, Rompin became the state's sole unhealthy locality after logging 141.
Conversely, parts of the Klang Valley showed slight improvement. Batu Muda and Cheras in Kuala Lumpur eased to 159 and 141, while Putrajaya improved to 118 from 151 in the morning. Petaling Jaya and Klang, which recorded 124 and 113 earlier in the day, dropped back into the moderate range.
Under the API system, readings between 101 and 200 are categorised as unhealthy. Health authorities advise high-risk individuals, including children, the elderly, and those with heart or respiratory conditions, to limit prolonged outdoor physical activity and wear face masks outside.

Title: Drunk driver crashes into DBKL road crew, killing supervisor on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A road maintenance supervisor was killed and a lorry driver injured early today when a suspected drunk driver crashed into them along Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 26-year-old driver recorded a breath alcohol level of 64mg/100ml, NST reported.
The suspect was arrested and remanded for three days until Monday to assist in investigations.
The crash occurred at around 5.00am when the car, travelling from Jalan Damansara towards Jalan Parlimen, lost control and struck two workers in the left lane.
"The victim, a supervisor, was pronounced dead while receiving treatment, while another worker, a 49-year-old lorry driver, sustained injuries to his head and right hand. The lorry driver is receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital. The car driver escaped uninjured.
"The five workers, comprising a supervisor, a lorry driver and three Bangladeshi workers, had been carrying out warning sign installation works under a Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) contract.
"The work began at 11pm on Oct 23 and ended at 4am today," he said in a statement.
Zamzuri said the case is being investigated under Sections 44(1)(b) and 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs causing death and injury.
Police have urged anyone who witnessed the crash to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or visit the nearest police station.

Title: End of the road: Sabah police nab Beverly Hills murder suspect wanted for over 17 years
Article:
PENAMPANG, Oct 24 — A 42-year-old murder suspect on the run for more than 17 years has finally been arrested in Sabah over a 2009 homicide in Penampang.
Penampang acting police chief Assistant Superintendent Arisanti Aziz said investigators detained the man at a house in Kolombong, Inanam on Thursday.
“The arrest followed our continuous efforts to track down the suspect and investigate the case,” she said in a statement today.
Police had sought the suspect over the death of a man in Beverly Hills, Penampang on April 11, 2009.
“The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years.
“If the death penalty is not imposed, the offender is also liabe to at least 12 strokes of the cane, subject to applicable legal provisions,” she said.
Arisanti added that the arrest demonstrates the police force’s commitment to combating crime, including solving cold cases and bringing long-sought suspects to court.

Title: Missing man found dead in locked car at Kajang supermarket car park
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A man who went missing five days ago was found dead inside a locked car parked outside a supermarket in Jalan Impian Mahkota late last night, ending a desperate search by his family that had circulated on social media.
Kajang district police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said authorities were alerted to the stationary vehicle at 11.29pm after passers-by spotted a motionless figure in the front cabin,
NST
reported.
"Initial investigations found a man, believed to be in his 50s, lying unconscious in the driver's seat of a Perodua Axia.
"The engine was off and the car was locked from the inside," he said.
Responding officers enlisted the help of the Fire and Rescue Department to pry open the locked doors, after which medical personnel from Hospital Kajang examined the victim and pronounced him dead at the scene.
Naazron confirmed that the victim's family had lodged a missing person report last Tuesday after repeated attempts to reach his mobile phone went unanswered. The vehicle was discovered approximately 15 minutes away from his residence.
"Preliminary investigations have so far found no foul play at the scene or on the deceased. The case has been classified as a sudden death report (SDR).
"Further investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the incident and his death," he said.
Yesterday, images circulated online showing police cruisers and fire rescue trucks cordoning off a vehicle in the supermarket car park.

Title: King and Queen offer prayers for late Terengganu prince Tengku Baderul Zaman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The King, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, and the Queen, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, have extended their condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire Terengganu royal family on the passing of Sultan Mizan’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
In a post on His Majesty’s official Facebook page, the King and Queen also prayed that the late Tengku Baderul Zaman’s soul be showered with barakah (divine blessings) and mercy, that all his sins be forgiven, and that he be placed among the faithful.
“Condolences to Al-Wathiqu Billah Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah and the entire Terengganu Royal Family on the passing of Dato’ Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
“Prayers are raised that the soul of the late Tengku Baderul Zaman be showered with barakah and mercy, that all his sins be forgiven, and that he be placed among the faithful,” the post read.
Tengku Baderul Zaman was reported to have passed away at 1.20 am today at a hospital in Kuala Lumpur. — Bernama

Title: PM extends condolences to Terengganu Sultan over brother’s death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, on the passing of His Royal Highness’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Allah SWT would shower His mercy upon Tengku Baderul Zaman’s soul, grant him forgiveness and place him among the righteous.
“May the Sultan of Terengganu and the entire royal family be granted fortitude and strength in facing this deeply felt loss. Al-Fatihah,” the post read.
Tengku Baderul Zaman died at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital here. — Bernama

Title: BN rejects Perikatan request for additional seats in Melaka election
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 24 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will stick to its agreement to allocate seven seats it is not contesting to Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the Melaka state election, despite attempts to secure additional seats.
BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the allocation had been agreed upon under a mutual agreement, which BN would honour.
“I have heard about efforts to seek additional seats, but we already have a pact, an agreement to allow them to contest the seven seats BN is not contesting, which we have left to PN’s component parties to distribute among themselves.
“That is the decision for now, and we will stand by what we have mutually agreed upon,” he told reporters after the Ulul Albab Huffaz Graduation and Excellence Appreciation Ceremony here today.
Yesterday, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man was reported as saying that PN hoped to hold negotiations to secure an additional one or two seats in addition to the seven announced earlier.
Ahmad Zahid had previously confirmed that negotiations on a political understanding with PAS had been finalised, with BN to contest 21 seats while the remaining seven would be allocated to PAS and its political allies.
The Election Commission (EC) has set October 31 for nomination, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling in the state election. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia stands ready to assist Yemen, backs renewed negotiations
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 24 — Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian assistance to Yemen, while urging all parties in the protracted conflict in the country to return to the negotiation table and look for a diplomatic solution.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia empathises with the suffering of the Yemeni people who have to endure the effects of the protracted civil war, including famine and hardship in getting basic necessities.
He said the matter was brought up by his counterpart, Yemen’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, who shared on the latest developments in the country via a phone call on Thursday.
“Malaysia stands ready to participate in any relief mission or deliver assistance to countries that require it, to the best of our ability,” he told reporters after handing over Deepavali festive contributions at the Rantau community hall here, today.
Mohamad said the conflict must be brought to an end as it brings no benefit to the estimated 22 million affected inhabitants and instead inflicts prolonged suffering.
In light of this, he urged foreign stakeholders to play a constructive role by returning to negotiation table to bring peace and prosperity to the people of Yemen.
He said diplomatic efforts need to be prioritised in order to prevent the conflict from dragging on and undermining regional stability. — Bernama

Title: Government to establish Veterans’ Day for MAF veterans
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The government plans to establish Veterans’ Day to honour the service and sacrifice of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a specific date for the celebration will be proposed to the Cabinet soon for the government’s approval.
“It will serve as a recognition, a formal acknowledgement that we honour veterans.
“It will also certainly foster closer ties and greater public appreciation for MAF veterans in our country,” he said at the opening ceremony of the 100th National General Assembly of the Malaysian Armed Forces Veterans Association (PVATM) here today.
Also present were Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman and PVATM president Datuk Sharuddin Omar.
In other developments, Mohamed Khaled said companies awarded major government contracts must provide job opportunities for MAF veterans to ensure they continue to have a place in the economy after completing their service.
He said the Ministry of Defence (Mindef) will monitor the implementation of the initiative to ensure veterans also benefit from these job opportunities.
On Tabung Pahlawan (Warriors’ Fund), he said collections have risen every year, reflecting public appreciation for the contribution of armed forces veterans to safeguarding the nation’s peace and security.
He said collections increased from RM1.3 million in 2023-2024 to RM2.19 million in 2024-2025 and RM3.35 million in 2025-2026.
He added that collections for 2026-2027 have so far reached RM4.35 million, against a target of RM5 million. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar calls for thorough investigation into detainee’s death in police custody
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly in police custody.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he had contacted Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to obtain further information on the case and ensure that updates on the investigation were conveyed to the deceased’s family.
He said he understood the family’s grief and anxiety as they awaited answers regarding Noorizwan’s death.
“I acknowledge the presence of the late Noorizwan’s family to submit an appeal letter to me today. I am deeply saddened by his passing and understand the family’s grief and anxiety as they await answers,” he said.
Anwar, who was scheduled to attend several programmes in Melaka today, said he had delegated his officers to receive the appeal letter and listen to the concerns raised by the family.
Media reports previously said police were still awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and the pathology findings to determine the actual cause of the man’s death on Oct 1.
Noorizwan was detained by the Cheras District Police Headquarters to assist in investigations under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, as well as Sections 457 and 379 of the Penal Code.
He was subsequently referred to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) on Sept 30 for treatment and was pronounced dead at 1.52 am the following day. — Bernama

Title: New-generation MyKad records 275,785 issuances in first month
Article:
KULAI, Oct 24 — The National Registration Department (JPN) has issued 275,785 new-generation MyKad nationwide since its launch on Sept 17 until Oct 20, with Johor recording the highest number at 31,392 cards.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures reflected a positive response from the public to the new-generation MyKad, which comes with enhanced security features.
He said the new-generation MyKad incorporates 53 security features, compared with 23 in the previous version, including a transparent window, QR code, ultraviolet features, hologram and microtext.
The enhancements were introduced to ensure the identity card’s security features remained relevant to technological advancements, following about 12 years of use of the previous MyKad generation.
“JPN has taken steps to further upgrade the security features. That is why we call it the new-generation MyKad,” he said.
“Johor recorded the highest number, with 31,392 cards issued, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 29,601, Selangor (26,736), Sarawak (25,642) and Sabah (22,523),” he told a press conference after officiating the 78th National Registration Day celebration and the launch of the Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School initiatives at the Kampung Melayu Sedenak Multipurpose Hall here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the public need not rush to replace their MyKad, as JPN had assured that the supply of cards was sufficient to meet demand.
He said about 24 million existing MyKads were currently in circulation, while JPN received an average of 200,000 applications a month for various purposes, including new identity cards, replacements for damaged cards and MyKad issuance to those turning 18.
He said possession of a MyKad was becoming increasingly important due to various government initiatives requiring its use, including purchases of petrol and cooking oil, as well as the redemption of Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA).
“We do not have any projections. We will continue as usual and serve the public. What matters is ensuring that the card supply is sufficient to meet demand from those who choose to switch to the new-generation MyKad,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Cheras custodial death: Family takes plea to PM’s doorstep, seeks transparent probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died earlier this month while under the custody of the Cheras district police, brought their fight for justice directly to the prime minister's doorstep this morning, demanding an independent and transparent inquiry into the circumstances surrounding his death.
Accompanied by legal counsel from rights group Lawyers for Liberty (LFL), the 42-year-old deceased's family arrived at Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's private residence in Bandar Sungai Long, gathering at the entrance before security personnel ushered them into the compound to deliver a formal protest memorandum to the prime minister's representative, NST reported.
The memorandum, handed over by Noorizwan's younger brother Nooranis Zulkefly, expressed profound alarm over unexplained physical injuries documented during the post-mortem examination, urging Putrajaya to intervene directly to prevent an institutional cover-up.
Pathologists at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) in Cheras confirmed that while the post-mortem detected no structural trauma to internal organs, Noorizwan's body bore multiple external contusions and injuries.
The formal medical cause of death remains uncertified and has been officially recorded as "pending laboratory analysis" while the Chemistry Department conducts specialised toxicological and histopathological tests.
Noorizwan was arrested by Cheras police personnel on Sept 19 under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, along with allegations of burglary and theft under the Penal Code.
Following 11 days in police lock-up, his physical condition deteriorated sharply, prompting authorities to transfer him to HCTM on Sept 30, where medical staff pronounced him dead in the early hours of Oct 1.
The family's petition follows public remarks by Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus, who defended the custodial administration by insisting officers followed standard operating procedures to the letter before the detainee took ill.
Fadil had publicly noted that Noorizwan held 44 prior criminal records, mainly related to narcotics and property theft, and had confessed to multiple break-ins in the Cheras district.
Bukit Aman's specialised Criminal Investigation and Deaths in Custody Unit (USJKT) has since expanded its internal affairs investigation, questioning 78 witnesses ranging from police personnel and medical specialists to legal aid representatives and the victim's immediate family.

Title: Police probe local syndicate links after Indonesia seizes tanker carrying RM800m ketamine off Sumatra
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Federal narcotics investigators are working in close concert with Indonesian law enforcement to determine whether a Malaysian drug syndicate orchestrated the trafficking of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine hydrochloride aboard a coastal tanker intercepted off North Sumatra.
The 57-metre Mongolian-flagged vessel, MT Global 168, was intercepted off Tanjung Balai Asahan on October 20 after Indonesian authorities linked its registered ownership to Johor-based firm Makmur Marine Petroleum.
A boarding search uncovered 58 sacks concealing 1,160 individually wrapped bricks of high-grade ketamine hydrochloride, with an estimated black-market street value of 3.48 trillion rupiah, or roughly RM800 million.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that Malaysian police were formally notified of the massive maritime interdiction by Indonesian counterparts yesterday,
NST
reported.
“NCID will remain in close contact with the Indonesian National Police to obtain further details of the case and exchange relevant intelligence.
“We will also seek information to determine whether any members of drug syndicates operating in Malaysia were involved,” he said.
Preliminary tracking data shared by Indonesian maritime agencies reveals that the tanker embarked from a docking yard in Pasir Gudang, Johor, before stopping to take on bunker fuel at Port Klang.
The vessel then plotted a course towards the open waters of the Andaman Sea, where regional surveillance units flagged anomalous navigation routes between October 14 and 18.
“The vessel was believed to have switched off its Automatic Identification System (AIS) for three days in an attempt to evade detection,” he said.
Hussein added that coastal radar picked up suspicious circular holding patterns off the western coast of Thailand immediately before the tanker turned back toward the Malacca Strait and Sumatran territorial waters.
Indonesian security personnel detained all eight crew members aboard the vessel, comprising seven Indonesian nationals aged between 25 and 71 and a 42-year-old Chinese national. All eight have been designated as formal criminal suspects.

Title: Kedah, Penang, Perak, Melaka, Johor and Sarawak put on thunderstorm alert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has sounded a midday thunderstorm advisory for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, warning of torrential rain, lightning, and gusty winds until 2.00pm today.
Issued at 11.00am, the weather alert focuses heavily on the northern corridor of the peninsula. In Kedah, stormy conditions are expected across eight districts, namely Kota Setar, Pendang, Yan, Kuala Muda, Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Baling, and Sik. The advisory concurrently blankets the entire state of Penang, as well as northern Perak localities spanning Selama, Kerian, and Larut Matang.
Further south in the peninsula, adverse weather is forecast to lash Melaka Tengah and Jasin in Melaka, alongside Tangkak and Muar in northern Johor.
cross East Malaysia, Sarawak accounts for the widest geographic coverage under the current bulletin. Affected zones include Sebuyau in the Samarahan division, alongside Pantu, Lingga, and Sri Aman within the Sri Aman division, and Betong. The advisory also extends into central and northern Sarawak, blanketing Selangau in Sibu, Mukah, Bintulu and Tatau in the Bintulu division, and Subis and Miri in the Miri division.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings when satellite and radar indicators detect rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist beyond an hour. The department noted that these short-term advisories carry a maximum validity of six hours from the time of release.
Members of the public across the affected localities have been advised to exercise caution against localised flash floods, sudden wind squalls, and falling branches or roadside trees during peak downpours.

Title: Wisma Putra: Two Malaysians suffer minor injuries after Typhoon Champi in Taiwan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals are currently receiving medical treatment for minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi on Taiwan, the Foreign Ministry said.
The ministry which is also known as Wisma Putra said the matter was confirmed by the Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre in Taipei, which is also providing the necessary consular assistance to both individuals.
“(The centre) remains in close communication with Malaysian student groups and the relevant local authorities to monitor developments and safeguard the welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan,” the ministry said in a statement on Saturday.
Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information concerning other Malaysian nationals who may require assistance in the affected areas, are urged to contact the Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre in Taipei at +886 972 349 343 or via email at
mwtaipei@kln.gov.my
.
Wisma Putra said it is closely monitoring the typhoon situation, which has brought strong winds and heavy rainfall. Adverse weather conditions are expected to persist in parts of Taiwan.
The typhoon has caused widespread flight cancellations and disruptions to ferry services. In light of this, Malaysians with upcoming travel plans are advised to check their flight or ferry status directly with the respective operators before proceeding to airports or terminals.
The ministry is advising Malaysians residing in or visiting Taiwan to monitor local weather advisories, avoid coastal and mountainous areas, and adhere to safety instructions and evacuation orders issued by local authorities.
It said local authorities have already evacuated residents from flood- and landslide-prone areas, including areas near a landslide dam in Hualien County. Malaysians are told to avoid unnecessary travel to such areas.
Wisma Putra is also encouraging all Malaysians to register and regularly update their contact details via the e-Konsular portal at
https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my
to facilitate timely communication and access to consular assistance.
— BERNAMA
TAGS: Typhoon Champi, Taiwan, Wisma Putra, consular assistance

Title: Perikatan seeks talks with Perlis MB Abu Bakar snookered by two-term Bersatu suspension
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) leadership is aiming to broker a resolution to the political crisis in Perlis, seeking direct talks with Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah following his two-term suspension from Bersatu.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan confirmed that he has officially written to Abu Bakar to request an urgent meeting to navigate the fallout from the disciplinary sanction and safeguard the stability of the state administration,
NST
reported.
"The discussions will focus on resolving ongoing issues, as PAS still supports the state government despite not being part of the state administration," he told a press conference following the Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah gathering in Kota Bharu last night.
Takiyuddin, who also serves as PAS secretary-general, noted that while Bersatu's disciplinary board had frozen Abu Bakar's party rights, the embattled state chief technically remains a Bersatu member.
He noted that this restricts Abu Bakar from seeking refuge outside of Bersatu.
"He cannot join another party, otherwise it would be party-hopping," he said.
Abu Bakar, who also heads the Kangar Bersatu division, was handed a two-election-term suspension after the party's disciplinary tribunal found him guilty of constitutional breaches. The punitive action sparked renewed questions over the viability of his leadership in the country's smallest state.
The crisis comes despite a royal intervention in June, when the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Putra Jamalullail, decreed that Abu Bakar should be given the necessary space and latitude to administer Perlis until the conclusion of the state legislative assembly's current mandate.
That royal guidance followed a fractious internal revolt last December, when five Bersatu assemblymen teamed up with three rebel PAS lawmakers to withdraw confidence from then-menteri besar Mohd Shukri Ramli of PAS.
The resulting reshuffle saw Bersatu wrest the menteri besar post for Abu Bakar, prompting an aggrieved PAS leadership to pull out of the state executive council entirely and leave the administration operating without formal PAS representation in government.

Title: Sultan Mizan’s brother passes away; Terengganu declares three-day mourning
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 24 — The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman, son of the late Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, passed away at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital, Kuala Lumpur. He was 51.
According to a statement by the Comptroller of the Terengganu Royal Household, Datuk Mohd Sophian Abu Bakar, the remains of Tengku Baderul Zaman will arrive at Sultan Mahmud Airport in Kuala Nerus at 1.15pm aboard a special aircraft.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, will receive the remains of the late Tengku Baderul Zaman.
The remains will be taken to the Balai Islam, Istana Syarqiyyah, for final respects before being laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum of Masjid Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, has declared three days of mourning commencing today, with the following dress protocol.
For Muslim men, a songkok wrapped with an inch of white cloth. For non-Muslim men, an inch of white cloth wrapped around the songkok, a three-inch-wide black cloth band around the left sleeve, and a black necktie.
For Muslim women, a white headscarf; for non-Muslim women, a three-inch-wide black cloth band around the sleeve.
Tahlil ceremonies will be held for three consecutive nights at the Balai Islam beginning tonight. — Bernama

Title: Monarchy provides stability above political differences, says Selangor Sultan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Although society has evolved, the fundamental role of a constitutional monarch remains unchanged, the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, said.
His Royal Highness said the Ruler had a responsibility to uphold the Constitution, preserve continuity and serve as a symbol of unity above political differences.
“The monarchy provides stability during times of change and reminds us that enduring institutions continue to play an important role in safeguarding national harmony,” he said in a special interview in conjunction with his 25 years on the Selangor throne.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the Constitution provided clear guidance on his responsibilities.
“My responsibility is to serve all the people of Selangor without favour or prejudice,” he said.
His Royal Highness noted that respect for constitutional principles, impartiality and fairness enabled the monarchy to remain a trusted institution for all citizens, regardless of their background or political beliefs.
The monarchy, he said, represented continuity, stability, service and responsibility.
“It reminds us that leadership carries obligations rather than privileges,” he said.
Sultan Sharafuddin said these values remained relevant because societies benefited from institutions that encouraged moderation, unity and respect for the rule of law. — Bernama

Title: Sultan Sharafuddin calls for AI training, responsible social media use, geriatric care for Selangor’s future
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Sultan of Selangor hopes future generations of Selangorians will be knowledgeable, compassionate, resilient, united and respectful of others.
His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said young people should strive for excellence without losing their sense of responsibility towards society.
“They should also understand that diversity is one of Malaysia’s greatest strengths. Mutual respect and understanding will remain essential to our continued harmony and progress,” he said in a special interview held in conjunction with his Silver Jubilee celebrations.
The Selangor ruler also advised young people to read news reports in depth before commenting, particularly on social media, rather than forming opinions based solely on headlines.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the younger generation had rightly placed importance on environmental sustainability and heritage preservation.
“Economic progress should never come at the expense of our natural environment or historical identity.
“Planning for future generations means protecting forests, rivers and green spaces while preserving our historical landmarks and cultural traditions. Development and conservation are not opposing goals; they should reinforce one another,” he said.
His Royal Highness also noted that education remained the foundation of long-term progress, particularly in preparing young people for a rapidly changing world.
“Artificial intelligence may not replace all jobs, but in many instances, people who are trained in AI will replace those who are not.
“Selangor must not lose out in this area. We must be ready for this, and I hope the state government realises it,” he said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also cautioned that the well-being of senior citizens must not be overlooked as Selangor moves towards becoming an ageing society.
The Sultan said healthcare services must evolve alongside demographic changes, while innovation should continue to strengthen the state’s competitiveness.
His Royal Highness proposed that Selangor strive to become the first state to establish a dedicated geriatric medical centre specialising in the health, care, prevention and treatment of conditions affecting older adults.
These include age-related problems such as falls, frailty, urinary incontinence and memory decline.
“We need to prioritise the overall quality of life of the elderly, including their safety, independence and balanced medication,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman: Post-mortem finds external injuries in Cheras custodial death, cause of death pending lab analysis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A post-mortem conducted on a 42-year-old man who died following detention by Cheras police revealed no damage to his internal organs but confirmed multiple external bodily injuries, federal investigators said today.
The formal medical cause of death remains undetermined and has been classified as “pending laboratory analysis” while pathologists await toxicology and histology findings from the Chemistry Department, the Royal Malaysia Police’s Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS) confirmed in a statement this morning.
The findings arrive amid intensifying civil society pressure, following calls by rights watchdog Lawyers for Liberty for the case to be treated as homicide rather than a routine sudden death, citing visible physical trauma observed on the deceased’s body.
Today’s police statement acknowledged the external injuries but stopped short of describing their severity, nature, or likely origin.
Bukit Aman’s specialised Criminal Investigation and Deaths in Custody Unit (USJKT) is leading the inquiry across multiple operational angles. The 78 individuals interviewed so far include arresting and lock-up police officers, attending hospital doctors, forensic medical specialists, representatives from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), civilian witnesses, and two immediate family members.
To ensure independent oversight, JIPS confirmed that the case has been formally referred to the Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) under Section 26 of the Independent Police Conduct Commission Act 2022, fulfilling mandatory reporting statutory requirements for fatalities in custody.
The timeline provided by JIPS states that Cheras district police originally arrested the man on Sept 19 on suspicion of drug possession under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, along with housebreaking and theft offences under Sections 457 and 379 of the Penal Code.
After 11 days in detention, he was transferred to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz UKM (HCTM) on Sept 30 for emergency treatment and was pronounced dead at 1.52am on Oct 1.
On Oct 15, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said that the detainee had been managed in strict compliance with standard operating procedures before suddenly falling ill.
Fadil also highlighted that the deceased carried 44 prior criminal records, consisting of 18 narcotics infractions and 26 other offences, and had allegedly admitted to 17 unsolved break-ins across Cheras.
JIPS director CP Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid reiterated that police will not make any compromise regarding operational misconduct or excessive force by personnel, pledging that investigators will act strictly in accordance with statutory regulations.
She also urged the public and advocacy groups to refrain from unverified online speculation while forensic pathologists complete their lab analysis.

Title: Haze creeps back: Seremban and Johor’s Larkin log highest API readings at 169
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Air quality deteriorated across several states this morning, with 21 monitoring stations breaching unhealthy thresholds on the Air Pollutant Index (API), according to the Department of Environment (DOE).
Data from the DOE's environmental monitoring dashboard at 10.00am showed that nearly a third of the country's 68 air quality stations registered readings between 101 and 200.
Another 41 stations recorded moderate air quality, while only six maintained good air levels. No location breached very unhealthy or hazardous benchmarks, and all monitoring stations remained fully operational online.
Southern states bore the brunt of the smog, accounting for the country's highest pollution levels. Seremban in Negeri Sembilan and Larkin in Johor shared the nation's worst reading at 169, followed closely by Nilai at 167 and Bandaraya Melaka at 164.
Johor emerged as the most severely affected state, with seven stations logged in the unhealthy bracket. Beyond Larkin, elevated readings were recorded in Batu Pahat at 163, Pasir Gudang and Tangkak at 162, Kluang at 159, Pengerang at 157, and Segamat at 155.
Melaka saw all three of its monitoring stations slip into the unhealthy tier, with Bukit Rambai recording 162 and Alor Gajah logging 157 alongside the state capital. Negeri Sembilan also recorded a clean sweep of unhealthy readings, with Port Dickson posting 152 to join Seremban and Nilai.
Across the Klang Valley, the haze lingered over both federal territories and suburban centres. In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda recorded 162 and Cheras registered 152, while Putrajaya touched 151. Readings across Selangor proved milder, with Petaling Jaya posting 124 and Klang logging 113, the lowest among all 21 affected stations.
In East Malaysia, transboundary smoke pushed three stations in Sarawak into unhealthy territory. The air monitoring station at IPD Serian recorded 154, followed by Sri Aman at 152 and Kapit at 151.
Under national ambient air quality guidelines, API levels between 101 and 200 are categorised as unhealthy. Health authorities advise high-risk groups, including young children, senior citizens, and individuals with cardiovascular or respiratory ailments, to avoid prolonged physical exertion outdoors and wear protective face masks if venturing outside.
